samples.summary: Table-cell "None" still passes `backgroundColor: ""` and is NOT covered by the new normalization — in the Yorkie path the old color survives in the CRDT
samples.evidence: The fix normalizes `''` only for `InlineStyle` (`normalizeStyleClears` is wired into `applyInlineStyle` and `applyStyleInTree`). The cell-style picker at docs-table-context-menu.tsx:230 calls `editor.applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: "" })`, which flows through `Doc.applyCellStyle` → `YorkieDocStore.applyCellStyle` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2410). There `merged = {...cell.style, backgroundColor: ''}` and `serializeCellStyle` (line 239: `if (s.backgroundColor) attrs.backgroundColor = ...`) drops the falsy value, so `tree.styleByPath(..., attrs)` — a merge-only op with no `removeStyleByPath` counterpart — leaves the previous `backgroundColor` attribute on the cell node. The local cache is then set to `''` (line 2434), so the cell looks cleared locally while peers and any reload still read the old fill: cache/CRDT divergence and a silently lost user action. This is exactly the #793 class of bug the change set out to fix, left in place on one of the call sites the accompanying lessons note counts (docs/tasks/active/20260817-docs-highlight-none-clear-lessons.md:13).

samples.summary: No read-side normalization: documents that already stored `backgroundColor=""` keep the dead value until the user happens to press "None" again
samples.evidence: `parseInlineStyle` uses `if ('backgroundColor' in attrs) style.backgroundColor = attrs.backgroundColor;` (line 178) and `serializeInlineStyle` uses `typeof style.backgroundColor === 'string'` (line 123), so an existing `''` attribute is read back as `backgroundColor: ''` and re-serialized verbatim. The write-path fix only helps on a *new* clear action, so pre-existing runs still never compare equal to unset (`normalizeInlines` cannot merge them) and export paths that test key presence still see a highlight. No migration/read normalization was added anywhere.

samples.summary: Behavior change: "Reset text color" now inherits the block's named-style color instead of rendering the plain default
samples.evidence: Previously `color: ''` was stored on the run and, being falsy, made the painter fall back to the default text color even inside a named style that defines a color. After normalization the key is removed entirely, so the named-style inline default (layered under the run style — see text-editor.ts:2879 `styleDefaultsAtCursor()` and the effective-style merge) shows through again. For a Heading whose style supplies a color, "Reset" now yields the heading color rather than the default one. This matches `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` semantics so it is likely intended, but it is a user-visible change not covered by any test in the diff.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. docs-table-context-menu.tsx:230 does call editor.applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: "" }); editor.ts:3413-3436 forwards the style unmodified (no normalizeStyleClears, which is wired only into block-helpers.ts:318 and yorkie-doc-store.ts:1878, both inline-style paths). In YorkieDocStore.applyCellStyle (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2410-2438) merged.backgroundColor becomes '', serializeCellStyle drops it because of the falsy check at line 239, and line 2430 issues only tree.styleByPath with no removeStyleByPath — the repo's own comment at 1873-1877 and the applyCellSpan removal branch at 2478-2482 confirm styleByPath is merge-only, so the previous backgroundColor attribute survives on the cell node. Meanwhile line 2434 writes the '' into the local cache, so the cell appears cleared locally while parseCellStyle (line 257) restores the old fill on reload/remote sync. This is a reachable, silently-lost user action plus cache/CRDT divergence — a correctness (data-loss/broken-invariant) defect. The todo's non-goal note (20260817-docs-highlight-none-clear-todo.md:44) is a task-scope statement, not a guard, and does not make the bug unreachable or non-blocking under this lens.
